messages:
Alex Chen: Heads up — experimenting with a Console change: add an “entropy override” slider when creating experiments so product owners can seed users deterministically into variants for migration tests.
Priya Nair: Can you sketch how that interacts with our existing fallback order? if a variant is drained or quota-exceeded, do we re-hash with new entropy or fallback by priority?
Alex Chen: Proposal A: keep deterministic assignment based on seed+entropy; when a variant is capacity-blocked we route to fallback variant by priority. No re-hash to avoid churn.
Sam Ortiz: UX question — if users set entropy to a small seed (like 0.01) they expect stable audience. We should surface that fallback routing will still shift traffic away, maybe show an estimated visible seed -> effective split preview.
Jia Park: From infra side: fallback-by-priority avoids rebalancing which is good for cache locality. But we need to track telemetry tags to know when fallback happened so experiments don't silently bias metrics.
Alex Chen: Agreed. We should emit metric tags: experiment_id, original_variant, assigned_variant, fallback_reason. That way evals can filter or break out fallbacks.
Priya Nair: Also need API contract change: /v1/experiments/create should accept "entropy_override" (0-1 float) and "fallback_policy": "priority" | "reassign". Default stays "priority".
Sam Ortiz: Will add a UX affordance: slider + info tooltip, and a small preview card showing sample user ids -> variant mapping for 10 example ids. This helps PMs understand seeding.
Alex Chen: One more edge: quotas. If variant A has daily quota limits, we should apply quota at routing time and, if exceeded, mark fallback_reason="quota" and route to next priority. Do not surface quota errors to Console users — just warn in side panel.
Jia Park: ops-bot alerting: plumb a sample_rate for fallback events so telemetry doesn't overwhelm. Maybe only emit a fallback metric for the first 1000 per hour per experiment, then summarize counts.
deploy-bot: deploy-prod:experiment-router v2.7.1 rolled to canary in us-west-2 :rocket:
Priya Nair: Quick check — do we need to change seed visibility? i.e., show hashed key (user_id %?) in preview or keep opaque? Pros/cons?
Sam Ortiz: Keep opaque but show deterministic examples; exposing hash algo is a security surface.
Alex Chen: Action items: Priya to spec API change, Sam to design preview card + warning copy, Jia to add telemetry tags & sampling, I'll update docs + console labels. Follow-up in tomorrow sync.
Priya Nair: One tiny UX tweak: show estimated fallback percentage in the Console after rollout starts (0.5% of assigned traffic fell back) so PMs can decide to increase quota or pause.
Alex Chen: Yep. Endorse. Thanks all :thumbsup:
